title: Per-model telemetry explorer with cohort swimlanes and rollout controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a compact, interactive explorer for per-model and per-route telemetry that combines cohort swimlane visualizations, token-level waterfall insights, and inline rollout controls. This ticket covers high-fidelity specs, interaction patterns, prototype flows, and a small front-end component library for the new panels.

Scope and deliverables:
- Main explorer view with time-synced panes: latency quantiles (P50/P95/P99), throughput (RPS), tokens-per-request distribution, cost-per-1000-tokens, and an anomaly score sparkline per cohort.
- Cohort swimlanes: rows represent cohorts (e.g., client, route, model-variant, prompt-template) with compact color-coded anomaly bands; click a lane to expand token-waterfall microtraces for that cohort.
- Rollout strip: top-level compact control that shows active rollouts (canary %, variant mapping), allows toggling canary off/on and triggering an immediate rollback, with confirmation modal and a telemetry query link.
- Drilldowns: from any chart you can open a microtrace (sampled) for the selected time window; links to the request-level raw trace in Observability.
- Cost attribution overlay: when enabled, overlays cost-per-token heatmap on latency chart to help spot cost/latency correlation.
- A/B comparison mode: side-by-side model-variant comparison; difference view highlights statistically significant deltas (bootstrap test) for P95 latency and token-efficiency.

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- Must remain legible at small canvas sizes (min 320px width). Use sparklines + condensed numbers for summary cards.
- Cohort rows should be limited to top 10 cohorts by request volume by default, with a secondary dropdown for full list. This keeps the swimlane compact and avoids visual noise.
- Anomaly scoring is computed server-side; design assumes scores are normalized 0-100. Avoid encoding raw p-values visually.
- Sampling: microtrace drilldowns use reservoir sampling with 1k sample cap per day — spec includes messaging and a sample-rate indicator.

Outcome: A set of UX specs and a clickable Figma prototype plus a short handoff doc for engineering that defines chart data contracts (time buckets, quantiles, token histograms, cohort keys) and required API endpoints for rollout controls.
comments: 2026-03-11 — Aisha Patel: Initial draft posted in Figma (link below). Focused on compact swimlane visual to enable quick root-cause without leaving the console.
2026-03-12 — Marco Rodríguez: Reviewed data contract with Infra team. Need additional fields: rollout_id, variant_label, cohort_key_hash to support URLable drilldowns. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-13 — Erin Liu (PM): Suggested adding an explicit 'SLO burn' indicator for each cohort. UX updated to include a small donut next to cohort label showing % of SLO consumed in time window.

2026-03-14 — Notes: Prototype PR created in GitHub for component shells: github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/2897. Backend telemetry API proposal: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TELEMETRY-2.0-API.
acceptance_criteria: Explorer loads under 500ms for default 24h window on staging data (perf target for front-end team).
Cohort swimlane shows top 10 cohorts and expands to show token-waterfall microtraces on click.
Rollout strip can toggle a canary variant off with a rollback confirmation and sends the correct POST /api/rollouts/{id}/rollback payload.
A/B comparison highlights deltas with a statistical significance marker and offers 'promote variant' CTA when P95 delta < 5% and cost delta < 2%.
Accessibility: color palette passes contrast for text and the anomaly hatch pattern is visible when color is not distinguishable.
Design tokens and component variants published in the console-ui storybook; figma prototype link included in links field.
design_notes: Visual language: compact cards with left-aligned cohort labels, right-aligned numeric summaries. Use small-multiples for quantile ribbons; token histograms use logarithmic x-axis. Interaction rules: time-range selection syncs across panes; hover shows coordinated tooltip (cohort, metric, absolute value, baseline delta). On rollout actions, show inline toast confirming API response and include a linked telemetry query to validate impact. Provide a second-level 'explain-anomaly' modal that surfaces top contributing dimensions (model-variant, prompt-template, region).
